appraisal_events.evidence: frémissait joyeusement... poussait un cri de ralliement... avec la même joie qu'un homme qui, perdu dans une forêt, lit... « Belvédère Casimir-Perier »; mots qui semblaient avoir pour lui... la même utilité que certaines épithètes commodes aux poètes latins; une conversation... dépourvue de chefs-d'oeuvre véritables, mais pleine de tableaux authentiques, médiocres et majestueux
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator repeatedly frames the duke's genealogical name-dropping as naive, reflexive, and formulaic (like metrical filler words), while conceding his conversation still has an overall grand aristocratic effect despite being intellectually mediocre.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Elle est stupide. Mais non, elle n'est pas si belle. C'est une réputation usurpée... elle m'est fortement antipathique. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The Turkish ambassadress disparages the princess's intelligence and beauty, but she has just been established as an unreliable, gossip-prone source, so the narrator frames this as personal antipathy rather than an endorsed judgment.

status_effects.explanation: His conversational habits are portrayed as naively pleased and formulaic, mildly diminishing his intellectual stature though not his social grandeur.
She is directly disparaged as stupid, overrated for beauty, and personally disliked, though the source's reliability is undercut by the narrator's framing.

ambiguities: The candidate 'la grand-mère' does not appear in this passage; the only near-match ('sa grand'mère Lucinge') refers to M. de Bréauté's own grandmother, not the narrator's grandmother, so no event was recorded for her.
'le narrateur' is present only as listening/observing consciousness enjoying a 'plaisir poétique' from the genealogical talk, not as a staged social participant, so he was not scored.

marquis de Bréauté appears only as one name among several in the duke's genealogical catalog (alongside Wurtemberg, Louis-Philippe, etc.); this reads as part of the broader characterization of the duke's speech rather than a distinct local movement for Bréauté, so he was omitted.

duc de Châtellerault's aborted anecdote, cut off by the duchess, seemed to concern defending M. de Luxembourg's reputation (part of the already-accepted Luxembourg-gossip thread) rather than constituting a distinct status effect on Châtellerault himself, so it was omitted.
